knowledgePattern: Follow repeated modulus folding and integrate the resulting pieces

hints.title: Sketch the first few updates
hints.body: Use |1−t|=|t−1|: lower the current graph by one, then reflect any part below the axis upwards.
hints.recap: A modulus of the output reflects negative heights while leaving nonnegative heights unchanged.
hints.pitfall: Apply each operation to the current graph, not to the original graph each time.
hints.pause: Sketch enough stages to identify what happens on consecutive unit intervals.

recall.reminder: A modulus of the output reflects negative heights while leaving nonnegative heights unchanged.

hints.title: Justify the repeating behaviour
hints.body: Examine the update separately for values above 1 and for values between 0 and 1. Track when a value enters the latter interval.
hints.recap: A recurrence pattern needs a reason that the next update preserves or repeats it.
hints.pitfall: A few numerical values alone do not establish the graph across every interval.
hints.pause: Prove the pattern on the whole integration interval, then calculate the area of each piece.

recall.reminder: A recurrence pattern needs a reason that the next update preserves or repeats it.

solution:
1. For x≥0, the starting value is x. Applying the update T(t)=|1−t| subtracts 1 whenever t≥1. Once 0≤t≤1, successive updates alternate t and 1−t.

2. Take an integer j with 0≤j≤99 and j≤x≤j+1. After j updates the value is x−j∈[0,1]. The remaining 100−j updates leave x−j when j is even, and 1−(x−j) when j is odd.

3. Thus on each unit interval the graph is a straight segment between heights 0 and 1, in alternating directions. Every segment contributes triangle area 1/2. There are 100 intervals, so the integral is 100/2=50. Answer D.
